text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Minister of Public Works and Housing Majali tours flood-hit region in the south. Three dead and another three people injured when bridge collapsed. Rains damaged roads, houses, olive trees and fruit orchards.
- Justice Minister Dughmi says list of people to be released under King Hussein's general amnesty will be presented to cabinet on Saturday.
- Economic sources say 1997 budget focuses on supporting the poor and increasing capital expenditure. No increases in state salaries.
- Parliamentary deputies to review today the resignation of deputy Nazeeh Amareen.
- Opposition parties to work for cancellation of first Israeli trade show in Jordan next month.
- Prime Minister Kabariti returns from Spain.
- Information Minister Muasher says 1997 budget will demonstrate transparency and contains no hidden surprises.
- Japan grants Jordan $11.3 million for improving water supplies to Greater Amman.
- Parliamentary sources expect deputy Nazzareen's resignation to be accepted if he doesn't withdraw it before the start of parliamentary session.
- Electricians held first meeting in Labour Ministry yesterday aimed at resolving last week's strike, but company board members absent from meeting.
- Jordan welcomes expected easing of Iraqi suffering when oil-for-food deal is carried out.
- Tug-of-war seen in the making over key draft laws in the economy, opposition wants thorough discussion before they are passed.
